evidence.A: Trace preservation for an effective colored-noise Gram must be independently justified; Frobenius normalization of H alone does not imply it.
evidence.M: 75 synthetic Gram cells, 19,200 random traceless perturbations, direct-H evaluation, 60-digit minimum-gap check, two-stage moving-frame checks.
evidence.P: Two-line eigenvector inequality and conditional Gaussian monotonicity.
evidence.R: No physical Munich channel inference, no exact ML SER extremum, no new geometry or performance advantage.

initial_failed_test.cause: The first test draft imposed an unregistered >1e-12 lower-gap requirement.
initial_failed_test.correction: Removed the unregistered practical threshold; the preregistered criterion was strict positivity verified at high precision.
initial_failed_test.scientific_claim_changed: No. The result is a strict mathematical gap, not a practically useful uniform tightening.

scope: fixed-trace Hermitian effective-Gram uncertainty; 75 synthetic cells; no physical Munich observations

two_line_theorem.interpretation: For every fixed-trace E, the separable union-upper endpoint is strictly unattainable for rank_one and qpsk_squared; circular_16psk jointly attains all pairwise endpoints. The uniform strictness bound can be numerically negligible.
